tasks.title: Requirement and task state machines, and requirement ids
tasks.description: Spec §3 (states), §7.2 (ids), NFR1. Pure transition functions for requirements (`submitted → [intake_drafting → awaiting_intent] → spec_drafting → awaiting_spec → … → complete | partial | escalated`) and tasks (`pending → planning → awaiting_plan → … → approved | rejected`, plus `failed`, `held`, `blocked`, `escalated`). Each transition is driven by an event; illegal transitions raise. State is derived by folding a requirement's events, so the same log always gives the same state. Requirement ids are `R-<yyyymmdd>-<4 hex>`, collision-checked against existing folders.

`rejected` and `failed` lead to `escalated`; a task whose dependency is `escalated` becomes `blocked`.
A requirement is `complete` when all tasks are approved, `partial` when some are approved and some escalated or blocked, `escalated` when none are approved.
New ids match `^R-\d{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}$`, use the local date, and a forced collision produces a different id.

`failed` and `rejected` move to `escalated` automatically; with a missing attachment they pass through `call_for_edit` first. `escalated` → `call_for_edit` (user's question) → `escalated` is legal; `call_for_edit` is not an attempt and doesn't change the attempt count.
